title: Go-to-Market Technical Evidence and Negotiation Playbook
author: Amelia Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook is a single-source, field-ready package for sales, solutions engineering, and account teams to accelerate pilot-to-production conversations for Redwood Inference. It combines a concise positioning narrative, competitive talking points, negotiated pricing guidance, a bank of short case vignettes, and a prospect-facing security & compliance FAQ. Use the sections below as modular assets when preparing decks, proposal annexes, or live technical reviews.

1) Positioning narrative (30-second / 3-minute / technical paragraphs)

- 30-second elevator: Redwood Inference gives engineering teams predictable, production-grade LLM inference with consistent latency, cost controls, and deployment choices (hosted, dedicated, private) so product teams can ship features without building inference infrastructure.
- 3-minute pitch: Customers choose Redwood when they need predictable per-token economics, strict SLA boundaries for customer-facing features, and the ability to run models across cloud and private environments with a single control plane. We combine an optimized GPU serving runtime (continuous batching, KV cache, quantization profiles) with rollout and observability tooling (per-model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, regression alerts) so product and platform teams can iterate safely.
- Technical paragraph (for platform engineers): The runtime auto-selects kernels and quantization strategies, supports transparent KV-prefetch caching, and exposes a routing layer for latency/cost tiering. Integrations: OIDC + SAML for SSO, KMS/HSM for key management, VPC peering for private control plane, and observability exports to Datadog/Prometheus. Typical SLOs we help customers meet: p99 < 300ms for short completions (<=64 tokens) on Dedicated pools and < 2x price-per-token vs unmanaged self-hosted solutions for steady workloads.

2) Competitive brief (one-pager language + rebuttals)

- Primary competitors to reference: Major cloud-managed LLM endpoints (CloudAI), single-vendor LLM APIs (LargeLLM Co.), and on-prem inference stacks (OpenServeOps).
- Redwood differentiators (one-line bullets):
  - Unified serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments (same API + rollout controls).
  - Cost levers exposed to developers: batching/caching profiles, quantization recommendations, routing policies.
  - Production-first tooling: token-level cost dashboards, eval-driven regressions, automated canary rollouts.

- Common competitive objections and rebuttals:
  - "We can get lower raw GPU cost by self-hosting." -> Rebuttal: True for peak GPU hourly price, but total unit cost (tokens) is a function of caching, batching, model variant selection, and operational overhead. We provide model + quantization profiles and automated batching to reduce per-token cost; typical win vs DIY is 1.3x–2x in production for RLHF-style workloads.
  - "Cloud provider is already our standard." -> Rebuttal: Redwood installs into customer VPCs or runs dedicated pools in preferred clouds. Our API and rollout model let you preserve cloud governance while reducing engineering lift.
  - "We need guarantees for latency and availability." -> Rebuttal: We offer SLA-backed Dedicated capacity, published latency baselines per model, and multi-region failover + automatic fallback to compatible model variants.

3) Field playbook: how to run a pilot (step-by-step)

1. Discovery (Sales + SE): capture QPS, token size distribution, peak concurrency windows, data residency constraints, and success metrics (latency p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, error budget).
2. Pilot design (SE): propose a pilot with one endpoint mapped to a representative route, recommend model family and quantization profile, and propose a traffic profile (e.g., 10% of production traffic or 50k tokens/day).
3. Proposal (Commercial): include a 30–90 day reserved trial for Dedicated or a hosted usage cap + commercial credit. Attach success criteria and rollback conditions.
4. Activation (Infra/Customer): confirm VPC peering or API key, deploy pilot model with canary rollout, enable token-level telemetry and prefix caching.
5. Evaluation (2–4 weeks): run the evaluation harness with customer prompt sets, collect metrics (latency, tokens, quality deltas) and run QA regressions.
6. Scale plan: based on observed KPIs, recommend throughput targets, autoscaling policies, and an economics model for committed capacity.

4) Pricing guidance and negotiation anchors

- Standard pricing levers: hosted per-token; dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit by GPU or vCPU equivalent); private deployment license + support.
- Example negotiation anchors (for pilot conversion):
  - Pilot credits: 1–3 months of Hosted credit (value $10k–$50k) tied to success criteria.
  - Trial Dedication: 1–3 node reserved pool at a discounted rate (50–70% of list) for 60–90 days to demonstrate SLOs.
  - On ramp discount: graduated discounts for multi-quarter committed usage (> 6 months).

- Pricing examples (illustrative; adjust with commercial team):
  - Hosted: $0.0005 per prompt token, $0.0010 per completion token for LLM-family-A; embeddings $0.0002 per 1k vectors.
  - Dedicated (monthly): entry reserved pool $12,000/mo per A100-equivalent node with autoscale burst at +25% at pay-as-you-go rate.
  - Private deployment: one-time license $75k + support tier (10%/yr) + per-node installation.

Negotiation tips:
- Anchor on measurable success metrics, not raw hours. Propose a 60–90 day SLA-backed pilot with explicit rollback if latency or quality targets are missed.
- Use the economics model: show token-level cost delta vs current approach. Include a sensitivity table demonstrating impact of batching and prefix caching.

5) Case vignettes (3 short, customer-facing stories)

- Fintech: A fintech analytics company reduced per-user inference cost by 45% after moving to Redwood Dedicated with prefix caching for repeated conversational workflows. They preserved PII controls via VPC Private control plane and met SOC2 requirements with audit logging.
- Marketplace: A two-sided marketplace used Redwood Optimize to enable aggressive batching during off-peak windows, reducing monthly inference spend by 38% while maintaining p95 latency for user-facing chat.
- Healthcare (regulated): A digital triage vendor adopted Redwood Private on-prem package; key win was KMS/HSM integration for PHI and a documented upgrade/rollback playbook that satisfied the customer's security team.

6) Security & compliance FAQ for prospects (short answers suitable for RFPs)

Q: Does Redwood store customer prompt or output data?
A: By default hosted logs are retained for 30 days for billing and observability; Dedicated and Private options provide configurable retention and can be configured to not persist prompts. We provide an exportable audit trail.

Q: What encryption is used for data in transit and at rest?
A: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 or cloud-provider-managed KMS for at-rest in hosted and dedicated; customer-managed KMS/HSM for Private deployments.

Q: Can we run the control plane in our VPC and keep inference on-prem?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane with optional on-prem inference runtime. Network diagrams, peering instructions, and an install checklist are provided during onboarding.

Q: Do you support SOC2 / ISO27001 evidence and audits?
A: Yes. Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and provides read-only evidence packages for customers under NDA. For higher assurance customers we offer custom attestation support via our security team.

Q: How are keys and secrets managed?
A: Integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM are available. Private deployments can use customer HSM appliances.

7) Proposal annex templates (snippets to copy into customer docs)

- Success criteria template (copyable):
  - Latency: p95 < 400ms for 95% of user-facing requests for route X.
  - Cost: unit cost per 1k tokens <= $X after caching and batching.
  - Reliability: 99.9% availability over 30-day window for the Reserved pool.
  - Quality: No more than 5% regression against baseline prompts measured with eval set Y.

- Rollback clause template:
  - If after the trial period the provider fails to meet the defined Latency or Quality criteria, Redwood will revert the customer to previous traffic routing and provide a remediation plan; commercial credits will be applied per agreed terms.

8) Deck & demo checklist (for SEs and AEs)

- Pre-demo: validate tokens/sample prompts with customer, ensure model variant configured, enable streaming in dev.
- Live demo: show latency metrics in real time, demonstrate token-level cost in the console, run a small regression test set and show eval dashboard.
- Post-demo: deliver a short technical appendix with model selection rationale and recommended quantization profile.

9) Decision table: when to recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

| Primary driver | Recommend |
|----------------|----------|
| Speed to value, low compliance needs | Hosted |
| Predictable throughput, SLA requirement | Dedicated |
| Regulatory controls, on-prem data residency | Private |

Appendix A: sample economics sensitivity table (copy into proposals)

- Inputs: base QPS, avg input tokens, avg completion tokens, batching factor, cache hit rate, node cost.
- Output: cost per 1k tokens, monthly spend at 100k tokens/day, ROI vs self-host.

Appendix B: checklist for security review board (for legal & infosec)

1. Confirm data retention policy in SOW.
2. Provide SOC2 evidence package under NDA.
3. Provide network diagram and VPC peering plan.
4. Confirm KMS/HSM key handoff process.
5. Agree on incident response SLA and contact list.
